static_findings.snippet: Python projects use **uv workspaces** (similar to pnpm workspaces for JS) with manual `project.json`
**Key Insight**: uv manages Python deps via workspace, Nx orchestrates tasks. Single `uv.lock` at ro
| Run all tests | `pnpm nx run-many -t test` |
| Generate JS/TS app | `pnpm nx g @nx/next:app name` |
| Generate JS/TS lib | `pnpm nx g @nx/js:lib name` |
| Init Python project | `cd apps/name && uv init` |

content.user_title: Manage Nx Monorepos with AI Assistants
content.value_statement: Large Nx workspaces are hard to understand, build, and coordinate across teams. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for project graphs, affected tasks, generators, caching, CI, and ownership.
actual_capabilities: Explains Nx project graph commands for dependency analysis, focused views, and affected project discovery.
Guides affected builds, tests, lint tasks, and run-many task execution.
Shows Nx generator usage for Next.js, React, Node, JavaScript, and TypeScript projects.
Describes local cache, Nx Cloud setup, cache inputs, and cache troubleshooting.
Outlines uv workspace integration for Python apps and shared Python libraries.
Includes team ownership, RFC, onboarding, and human-AI task routing references.
limitations: Does not install Nx plugins or dependencies by itself.
Requires an existing workspace or user permission before running commands.
Provides examples that may need adjustment for package managers and repository policies.
Does not replace human review for security, architecture, or production deployment decisions.

use_cases.title: Modernize a Frontend Workspace
use_cases.description: Plan Nx generators, shared libraries, cache settings, and affected checks for Next.js or React projects.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Monorepo Ownership
use_cases.description: Use CODEOWNERS, RFC steps, and routing guidance to organize human and AI work.

use_cases.title: Add Python Services to Nx
use_cases.description: Map uv workspaces into Nx project tasks for testing, linting, building, and dependency sharing.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect My Workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Nx workspace structure. Explain the projects, likely owners, and the first safe commands to understand the graph.

prompt_templates.title: Run Affected Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose the correct Nx affected commands for this change set. Include build, test, lint, and base branch choices.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Shared Packages
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a shared library plan for these apps. Recommend Nx generators, naming, ownership, cache targets, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize CI and Governance
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Nx monorepo process. Improve CI, cache strategy, CODEOWNERS, RFC flow, and human-AI task routing.

output_examples.input: I need to understand dependencies before changing authentication.
output_examples.output: A graph-first review plan that identifies affected apps, owner groups, risk areas, and validation tasks.

output_examples.input: Our CI runs every task on every pull request.
output_examples.output: An affected-only CI approach with cache guidance, base branch checks, and verification steps for task coverage.

output_examples.input: We want to add a Python service to an Nx repo.
output_examples.output: A setup checklist for uv workspace membership, Nx project targets, dependency sync, and project graph validation.

best_practices: Start with project graph and affected checks before changing shared packages.
Use dry runs for generators before creating applications or libraries.
Keep ownership, CI, and cache rules documented in the repository.
anti_patterns: Running every task for every pull request without checking affected projects.
Adding generated projects without owners, cache targets, or validation steps.
Letting AI make architecture, security, or deployment decisions without human review.

faq.question: What tools does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code for Nx monorepo guidance.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides command guidance. Users should approve execution and review results.

faq.question: Can it help with Python projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains uv workspaces with Nx project targets for Python apps and libraries.

faq.question: Does it require Nx Cloud?
faq.answer: No. It covers local cache and optional Nx Cloud remote caching.

faq.question: Can it generate apps and libraries?
faq.answer: It guides Nx generator usage and recommends dry runs before changes.

faq.question: Is it safe for production deployments?
faq.answer: It states production deployments and security-critical changes require human approval.
